newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's economy expands 7.2 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Chile's economy expands 7.2 percent in 1996.

text.p: Chile's gross domestic product grew 7.2 percent last year compared with 1995, said the Central Bank in its fortnightly report.
The figure showed economic growth slowing from 8.5 percent registered in 1995. The bank said the economy grew 7.7 percent in the last quarter of 1996 compared with the same period in 1995.
"In general terms the level of economic activity was driven equally by internal and external demand," said the report.
"With this (annual) figure, the gross domestic product has accumulated an average increase of 7.4 percent in this decade."
Internal demand grew 7.9 percent last year with exports of goods and services climbing 10.9 percent compared with 1995.
"This last figure occurred despite an unfavourable international context as the result of the significant fall in the prices of export products," it said.
Private consumer spending grew a strong 8.8 percent last year, but this was "significantly less than its rate of expansion in 1995."
Areas which showed strongest growth last year included mining, up 12 percent and trade and construction which both rose 10 percent.
"Beneath this was the financial services sector with growth similar to the economy," said the report.
"Other sectors achieved growth of less than four percent, with the public administration sector showing the lowest growth of 1.4 percent."
The agriculture sector showed second lowest growth with output up just 1.5 percent.
